# dtcloud_snapshot (Resource)

Manages a point-in-time copy of a volume.

Size and storage policy come from the source volume at the moment the copy is taken, so only `name`
and `description` change in place. Restoring is not done here: a restore produces a volume, so it
belongs to `dtcloud_volume` through `source_snapshot_id`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "dtcloud_snapshot" "nightly" {
  name        = "app-data-2026-01-31"
  volume_id   = dtcloud_volume.data.id
  description = "Before the schema migration"
}

# Restoring is not done here: a restore produces a volume, so it belongs to the
# volume resource.
resource "dtcloud_volume" "restored" {
  name               = "app-data-restored"
  size               = 100
  storage_policy     = "standard"
  source_snapshot_id = dtcloud_snapshot.nightly.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the snapshot. Can be changed in place.
- `volume_id` (String) ID of the volume to snapshot. The volume may be attached to a running machine. Changing it takes a new snapshot and destroys this one. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free-text description. Removing it from the configuration clears it on the platform — the API expresses that as a JSON null, since it rejects an empty string outright.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the snapshot was taken, as the platform reports it. The API sends no timezone, and the value is passed through unchanged.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `progress` (String) How far the copy has got, as a percentage string such as `100%`. The only visible sign that a large snapshot is still being written.
- `project_id` (String) ID of the project the snapshot belongs to.
- `size` (Number) Size in GB, inherited from the source volume. A snapshot cannot be resized; it is as large as the volume was when it was taken.
- `status` (String) Status reported by the platform. `available` is the only resting state.
- `storage_policy` (String) Name of the storage policy backing the snapshot, resolved from `volume_type_id`. Empty if the storage-policies endpoint could not be read.
- `updated_at` (String) When the snapshot's metadata last changed. Empty until it is first renamed or re-described.
- `volume_type_id` (String) ID of the volume type backing the snapshot, as the snapshots endpoint reports it. `storage_policy` is the same thing by name.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String)
- `delete` (String)
- `update` (String)

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **The source volume may be attached and running.** The copy is of the block device as it is at
  that instant, so it is not a consistent filesystem. If the data matters, quiesce the application or
  take the snapshot with the machine stopped.
* **`description` round-trips, unlike a volume's.** It is read back, so it drifts, survives an import,
  and removing it from the configuration clears it on the platform. Create accepts no description,
  so one is applied by a second call.
* **`storage_policy` is resolved by the provider.** The snapshots endpoint reports only
  `volume_type_id`, so the provider looks the name up once per run and shares the answer between
  every snapshot. The lookup is best-effort: if it fails, `storage_policy` stays empty for the rest of
  the run, while `volume_type_id` is always set.
* **Deleting a volume deletes its snapshots.** Destroying the source `dtcloud_volume` removes every
  snapshot of it, managed by Terraform or not, and Terraform does not warn about it. With both in
  one configuration, the reference in `volume_id` makes Terraform destroy the snapshot first.
* **Deleting a snapshot can be refused** while it is still being created, or while a volume restored
  from it still depends on it. The platform's message is passed through; destroy the dependent volume
  first.

## Timeouts

`create` defaults to 30 minutes, `update` to 15 minutes and `delete` to 20 minutes. Creating copies
the whole volume, so the default is generous; raise it for large volumes. Override them with a
`timeouts` block:

```terraform
resource "dtcloud_snapshot" "nightly" {
  # ...

  timeouts {
    create = "1h"
  }
}
```

## Import

```shell
terraform import dtcloud_snapshot.nightly 9e7d3a02-5c81-4f6b-b294-7a1e6c4d8b55
```

Everything is read back, `description` included, so a plan straight after an import is empty when
the configuration matches the snapshot.
